audit.title: Key Terms and Concepts

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. Every term leads with its definition ("A 32-byte identifier that uniquely represents an entity across multiple EVM blockchains"), no back-references.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong chunking (median 42 words/section, max 76, none over 600), but the page skips H2 entirely (H1 → 50× H3), the one measured level skip. No grouping headers or index table to aid navigation.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Good for a glossary: `bytes32`, `keccak256("common.kyc")`, ERC-20/165/3643, EIP-712, 32-byte. Weakened by 0 numerals carrying units and the vague quantifier "most."

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 71 links (67 internal, 4 external); heavy, correct internal cross-linking. Only 1 primary source (github crec-sdk) plus one Wikipedia ISO link; ERC/EIP standards are named but not linked to their specs.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. Crisp one-to-two-sentence definitions are the page's entire purpose and are cleanly liftable.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no `dateModified`/`inLanguage` in head, 0 og/twitter tags. A visible "Last Updated: 2026-07-17" exists in body but not as machine metadata.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: 0 fenced blocks; appropriate for a glossary, and inline code (`transfer(address,uint256)`, `runPolicy`) is used well. Scored mid because the content type doesn't demand runnable snippets.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Term headings map well to "what is X" queries, and coverage of the ACE lifecycle is broad. No acronym-expansion aliases in headings for symptom/abbreviation search, no FAQ/troubleshooting angle.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Clean and consistent overall, but the CRE Connect Wallet definition reads circularly: "Your wallet owns the CRE Connect Wallet, and the CRE Connect Wallet owns all your ACE contracts."

audit.summary: This is a well-built ACE glossary: 50 term sections, each opening with a self-contained, quotable definition and densely cross-linked to concept pages — near-ideal structure for RAG chunking and verbatim citation. Its single biggest strength is answer-first extractability; every H3 is a coherent, standalone retrievable unit. Its single biggest opportunity is machine-readability: with zero JSON-LD, no canonical URL, and no head-level dates, a glossary that is textbook material for `DefinedTermSet`/`DefinedTerm` schema is leaving structured-data lift on the table. Honest verdict: strong content, under-instrumented for machines.

recommendations.title: Add `DefinedTermSet` / `DefinedTerm` JSON-LD
recommendations.issue: "JSON-LD: 0 block(s)" — glossary has no structured data.
recommendations.change: Emit one `DefinedTermSet` with each term as a `DefinedTerm` (`name`, `description`, `url` anchor). This is the schema type purpose-built for glossaries and directly exposes each definition to engines.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata raises parse-trust and lets engines cite individual terms as canonical definitions rather than skimming prose.

recommendations.title: Add canonical URL and head-level dates
recommendations.change: Add `<link rel="canonical">` to the page URL and a `dateModified` (2026-07-17) matching the visible body date; set `inLanguage`.
recommendations.why: Freshness and canonical signals feed E-E-A-T and prevent duplicate-URL dilution during retrieval.

recommendations.title: Fix the heading level skip / add H2 grouping
recommendations.change: Introduce H2 grouping headers (e.g. "Platform & APIs", "Identity & Credentials", "Policies & Enforcement", "Standards") with terms as H3 under them, or alphabetical H2 buckets.
recommendations.why: Removes the skip and gives engines a clean hierarchy for section-level retrieval and disambiguation.

recommendations.title: Link ERC/EIP standards to primary specs
recommendations.issue: Standards named but only 1 primary-source link on the page.
recommendations.change: Inline-link each to its canonical spec (eips.ethereum.org / ERC-3643 spec) alongside the existing internal reference links.
recommendations.why: Primary-source citations raise credibility and citation rate for standards-related answers.

recommendations.title: Repair the circular CRE Connect Wallet definition
recommendations.issue: "Your wallet owns the CRE Connect Wallet, and the CRE Connect Wallet owns all your ACE contracts."
recommendations.change: Name the owning entity explicitly (e.g. "Your organization's owner wallet owns the CRE Connect Wallet, which in turn owns all your ACE contracts…").
recommendations.why: Removes an ambiguous entity chain that risks an inverted synthesized ownership answer.

recommendations.title: Add acronym aliases to acronym-heavy headings
recommendations.where: CCID, DON, KYC, AML, PII, PoR headings (already expand inline)
recommendations.issue: Symptom/abbreviation queries ("what is a CCID chainlink") rely on body text.
recommendations.change: Keep expansions in the heading (already done for most) and ensure the first sentence restates the acronym verbatim; consider adding "PoR" alias next to "Proof of Reserve."
recommendations.why: Matches how devs actually query by abbreviation, improving retrieval hit rate.

recommendations.title: Replace the vague quantifier
recommendations.where: Mapper entry ("In most cases, the PolicyEngine's built-in… is sufficient")
recommendations.change: Specify the condition ("Name-based mapping is sufficient unless parameters must be transformed or combined before evaluation").
recommendations.why: Concrete conditions outperform qualitative hedges in extracted answers.

antiPatterns: Heading level skip (H1 → H3) — see P2.
One circular/ambiguous entity definition (CRE Connect Wallet) — see P2.
Vague quantifier "most" in the Mapper entry — see P3.
No keyword stuffing, marketing fluff, unresolved cross-references, or stale content detected; internal anchors resolve to real terms.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at page top — good; confirm the glossary and its anchors are indexed there.
Head metadata could not be verified from the served HTML ("none captured"); the CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read before treating schema/canonical as truly absent.
Site-level: ensure `TechArticle`/`DefinedTermSet` emission is templated across all `ace/concepts` pages, not patched per-page.
